thread:
Ravi S: Quick per diem Q - traveling to APAC for client work. Outbound is an overnight red-eye, arrive 06:30 local, full meeting day that evening where client covers lunch and a working dinner. Return is a late-afternoon flight that gets me home the same calendar day. How do we count per diem for the arrival and departure days?
Jordan (People Ops): Short answer: per diem is prorated by company policy for partial travel days. Arrival day counts as 75% if travel occurs during the majority of the day; departure day counts as 50% if you depart before noon, otherwise 75% on travel policy. But we also deduct meals provided by client.
Ravi S: So for arrival: I land at 06:30, meetings run 09:00-17:00, client provides lunch and working dinner. Is that 75% minus 2 meals? That seems odd.
Finance Bot: Policy excerpt: Arrival/Departure proration rules: - Full day = 100% - Partial day (arrival before 08:00 or after 20:00) = 75% - Short travel day (arrival between 08:00-12:00 or depart before 13:00) = 50% Meal offsets: deduct per diem meal allowances when a meal is provided and itemized. For multi-meal days, per diem is reduced by proportionate meal allowances.
Travel Desk (Amelia): Practical approach: record arrival day as 75% per diem, then subtract client-provided lunch and dinner (two meal offsets). Upload the client agenda/email confirming meals.
Ravi S: How do I show the math in Expensify? Is there a special field or do I need to attach a manual calc?
Jordan (People Ops): Put one expense line "Per diem - Arrival (75%)" for the arrival day and one for "Per diem - Departure (50%)" for the return day. In the expense comment box show the calculation, e.g., "Arrival: 75% of $60 = $45; minus lunch $12 and dinner $18 => reimbursable $15." Attach client agenda/email as proof of meals. Finance will validate.
Nora - Events: For sponsor/client-covered meals, we ask the client to provide an itemized receipt or confirmation email. If it's a group working dinner on their tab, an email from the client rep is fine.
Ravi S: Currency: client invoice is in JPY and per diem table uses local JPY rates. My card charged some incidental parking in USD. Any special handling?
Finance Bot: Record amounts in original currencies and attach card statement. Expensify will convert; include a manual note with your card exchange rate if you want. VAT/GST: if recoverable, Finance will process reclaim when receipts include tax lines.
Ravi S: Cool. One weird edge: the working dinner finished after 21:30 local but was 'provided' as a buffet on-site with no itemized invoice. Client only sent a note saying "dinner provided". Is that enough?
Jordan (People Ops): For non-itemized meal confirmations, we accept client email plus event agenda. If Finance needs more, they may reach out. Add the client note and agenda to the expense.
Travel Desk (Amelia): Also FYI: if your itinerary crosses midnight and you depart before 13:00 local on departure day, choose 50% proration per policy. If rounding ambiguity, People Ops will make a call to keep it simple.
Ravi S: Thanks. I'll file two per diem lines with calculations and attach the agenda + client confirmation + card stmt. Tag it "per-diem-apac" and flag for manual review.
Finance Bot: Received. Automated check: flagged for manual review due to meal offsets. Expect response in 2 business days.
Ravi S: Appreciate it, thanks everyone :grin:
